title: Enterprise Access buying-path experiments for SSO/SAML and granular RBAC commitments
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Enterprise procurement teams often ask for firm commitments around SSO (SAML) availability and a clear RBAC model in contract terms. We need to test packaging variants that balance commercial commitments against engineering/ops cost and product scope. Scope: run two buying-path experiments for mid-market and enterprise segments to validate willingness-to-pay for contractual SSO/SAML SLAs and for tiered RBAC entitlements (basic role sets vs. advanced custom roles + audit logs). Deliverables: experimental pricing pages, sample contract language, legal sign-off checklist, and telemetry to measure conversion and churn impact.
acceptance_criteria: Two live pricing/contract variants published in the self-serve checkout and sales playbook
Legal-approved SLA language for SSO availability and RBAC commitments stored in Confluence
Experiment metrics dashboard tracking MQL -> closed-won conversion, time-to-contract, deal-size delta, and support tickets for access/SCIM issues
Decision point documented with recommendation to scale, iterate, or sunset within 8 weeks of experiment start
steps: Draft contract language and entitlement matrix with Legal and Security (week 1)
Implement two pricing variants in checkout microsite and sales playbook: Variant A (SSO as configurable add-on) and Variant B (SSO + advanced RBAC bundled with premium tier)
Coordinate with Eng to scope minimal RBAC enforcement and audit logging required for Variant B; surface upgrade path for Dedicated/Private customers
Run sales enablement and support training; publish FAQ and runbook for on-boarding SSO/SAML
Launch experiment to targeted accounts and track via dashboard (8 weeks)
Analyze results and collect qualitative feedback from 10 pilot customers and AE debriefs
notes: Trade-offs: a strict contractual SLA for SSO uptime increases operational overhead and could force reserved capacity constraints under Dedicated plans.
We must avoid promising RBAC features we cannot fully support on Private deployments without upgrade windows; propose migration clause.
Consider a measurable SLA that excludes customer-managed network outages for Private/VPC customers.
Reference: previous contract-playbook experiments showed a 12% deal-size uplift when security features were bundled (PM-27489, PM-21847).

risks: Operational cost risk if many customers take bundled RBAC - may require Dedicated capacity scaling
Legal risk from over-committing SSO uptime without runbook/monitoring agreement
Reputational risk if SAML flows are brittle and lead to onboarding failures
measurement_plan: Primary metric: closed-won rate among targeted cohort over 8 weeks (baseline comparison)
Secondary metrics: average ACV, time-to-signature, number of SSO support tickets created within 30 days of onboarding
Qualitative: AE and customer interviews documenting blockers and competitive feedback
